content:
morgan: heads-up — I ran the group-size sweep with AWQ vs GPTQ on the 7B fp32->int8 weight-only path. surprising perf cliff at group=16 for some kernels.

kai: saw that too. is the cliff across all sequences or just short chats?

morgan: mostly < 128 tokens. Medium/long sequences look fine; latency per token jumps for batch sizes <=2 and group=16.

sana: could be kernel selection fallback hitting a non-optimal path for small microbatches. which kernel names did profiler show?

morgan: profiler: 
```
selected_kernel: awq_int8_group16_v2
fallback_kernel: awq_int8_generic
launch_ms: 0.45 -> 1.9
avg_token_ms: 4.8 -> 7.3 (microbatch 1)
```

leo: that launch_ms jump smells like increased kernel workspace + memcpy overhead for group-aligned packing. maybe we trigger an extra unpack step when kvcache misaligns?

priya: i replayed traces with KV hits annotated. when group=16 we see more KV evictions on the slab allocator, eviction rate ~2.1% vs 0.3% for group=32. so KV cache thrash might expose an unpack path.

morgan: interesting — eviction correlates with perf cliff. could be packing expansion increases working set and pushes LRU out.

kai: what about calibration? did we reuse the same per-group scale params across sequence lengths? AWQ calibration we ran on 64-token windows; maybe scale estimates are off for short prompt distributions -> different sparsity pattern -> memory layout changes.

morgan: calibration note: AWQ calib used per-tensor scale with fallback histograms. i also tried recalib on 8-token slices and the kernel chooser stayed with the optimal kernel. latency recovered.

sana: so calibration hysteresis (calib data distribution mismatch) changed packing density, which changed kernel selection -> KV cache footprint -> eviction -> fallback kernel -> perf regression. chain reaction.

leo: any quick mitigation? tune batching heuristics to prefer microbatching with group-size aware padding? or force kernel selection to prefer low-launch-overhead path for batch<=2?

priya: we tested a heuristic: prefer awq_int8_smallbatch kernel when batch<4 regardless of predicted throughput. result: median p95 latency down 18% on our chat traces, cost +1.2% tokens.

morgan: logs for heuristics test: 
```
2026-01-28T14:03:12Z INFO routing: forced_kernel=awq_int8_smallbatch reason=batch<4
2026-01-28T14:03:12Z DEBUG kvcache: pre_usage=78MB post_est=81MB eviction=0
2026-01-28T14:03:12Z PERF token_ms=5.1 p95=12.3
```

kai: good pragmatic short-term fix. long-term we should: (1) add a calibration sanity check that tests multiple context lengths, (2) surface packing-induced kv footprint estimate to the kernel selector, (3) let autoscaler/allocator co-optimize for quant packing.

morgan: agree. i've opened a small RFC with proposed changes + perf tests. comments welcome: https://rwd/internal/rfcs/awq-group-kv-handoff (stub link).

profiling-bot: upload complete: /artifacts/profiler/1733334444/group16_vs_32_awq_gptq.tar.gz

priya: uploaded artifacts look clean. next step: run the A/B on dedicated nodes (to rule out noisy neighbors) and if stable, patch the kernel chooser to include "estimated_kv_delta" in score.

sana: i'll take the A/B on dedicated infra. assigning to me until EOD.

morgan: thanks — will draft the kernel-chooser patch and add a quick feature flag. if A/B fails we'll roll the flag back. :thumbsup:

kai: small ask — add a test that fails if calibration produces >1.5x delta in estimated working set between calib-distributions. helps catch future hysteresis.

morgan: done, added unit + integration test in the RFC.

priya: great. sync in 2 days after A/B.

morgan: thanks all.
